title: Continuous stream admission guard and kernel steward
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: We observe infrequent but high p99/p999 latency spikes for continuous batching workloads (chat/prefill heavy). Root causes appear to be suboptimal kernel choices for mixed-sequence batches and late-arriving long-prefill requests that break batch shape assumptions. Goals: 1) reduce p99 by 30% for mixed-length workloads at 95th percentile load; 2) limit average token-cost regression to <3%; 3) make admission decisions transparent and tunable per-tenant.
proposal_summary: Implement an admission guard that blends token-aware deadline admission with a kernel steward that tracks recent kernel latency distributions per model-sequence-shape. The admission guard will apply lightweight micro-slicing for long-prefill arrivals and opportunistic coalescing for short-prefill bursts. The kernel steward will surface a ranked list of kernel variants and a predictive selector that prefers lower-variance kernels for tail-sensitive lanes.
success_metrics: p99 latency reduced by 30% on mixed-length traces
p999 latency reduced by 40% under steady-state load
no functional changes to output correctness
work_items: Instrument per-kernel running histograms keyed by (model,seq_len_bucket,kernel_variant)
Add admission_guard component to prefill path with token-deadline budgeting
Implement micro-slice prefetch: split long prefill into head-slice + tail-slice with separate admission budgets
Add kernel_steward service to recommend kernel per admission decision
Expose per-tenant tuning knobs in Console (max_head_slice_ms, tail_coalesce_threshold)
tests_and_validation: Synthetic mixed-length traffic replay (700k tokens/day) comparing baseline vs patch
A/B canary on Dedicated pool w/ 10% traffic for 48h
Unit tests for admission budget math and kernel-steward heuristics
Perf CI that measures p50/p95/p99 across representative shards
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gated behind runtime flag; CI perf baseline established. 2) Canary on internal dev cluster (low priority tenants) for 24h. 3) Canary on Dedicated pooled infra (10% traffic) and monitor p99/p999 and OOMs for 48h. 4) Gradual 25/50/100% rollout with circuit breaker to revert on regression. 5) Post-rollout bake and telemetry review.
risks: Incorrect kernel ranking could increase avg token latency for some shapes
Micro-slicing adds scheduler complexity and may increase total GPU work if mis-tuned
Per-tenant knobs could be misused and cause unpredictable SLAs
open_questions: How to set warm-start priors for kernel latency distributions for newly onboarded models?
Should kernel_steward be a centralized service or sharded per-runtime instance?
What default knobs are safe for self-serve tenants vs enterprise tenants?
acceptance_criteria: Automated canary shows p99 improvement >= target on representative traces
No more than 3% token-cost regression across tested workloads
Feature flags and console knobs are available and documented
Perf dashboards updated with kernel-level histograms and admission events
